title: Why Do Only Your Fingers Wrinkle?
pause_note: 'long' lists beat indices followed by a pause; Short: 0.6 s

beats: Why do only your fingers and toes wrinkle in water?
Your arms and your back stay smooth. Only fingertips and toes turn into prunes.
Most people think the skin just soaks up water. That's not the whole story.
In the 1930s, doctors noticed something strange. Fingers with a damaged nerve didn't wrinkle.
Same skin, same water. No nerve signal, no wrinkles.
Here's how it seems to work. The nerve tells blood vessels in the fingertip to narrow.
The fingertip loses a little volume, and the skin on top folds into wrinkles.
So it isn't just soaking. Your nervous system is making them wrinkle.
Why? Scientists are still arguing about that.
